answer: Generator calculators size a set for what must run during a power cut: the running watts of everything on at once plus the starting surge of the largest motor, turned into kVA with the power factor and rounded up to a size that is sold. They also show what a given kVA can run and what it costs in fuel.

sections.h2: Which generator calculator do I need?
p: For a whole home, start with the [[C1|generator size calculator]]; for a list of appliances, the [[C2|generator watts calculator]]. If a motor or compressor is on the list, the [[C3|starting watts calculator]] and the guide to [[C4|running vs starting watts]] show why it sets the size.

For one big load, use the [[C5|generator size for a well pump]] or the [[C6|generator size for an AC]]. If you already own a set, [[C7|what a generator can run]] turns its kVA into usable watts, and the [[C8|fuel consumption calculator]] gives the litres and rupees an hour.

sections.h2: Why the starting surge decides the size
p: Running watts are what an appliance draws while it works; a motor or compressor draws several times that for a second or two as it starts. In the default home on the generator size calculator the running load is {{pg.C1.out.running_w|int}} W but the peak is {{pg.C1.out.peak_w|int}} W, which is why it needs {{pg.C1.out.standard_kva|1}} kVA. Starting one motor at a time keeps the peak, and the generator, smaller.

faq.q: What size generator do I need for my house?
faq.a: {{pg.C1.out.standard_kva|1}} kVA for a typical home with fans, lights, an inverter fridge, a TV, one inverter AC and a water motor. More ACs or a non-inverter AC need more; enter your own list in the [[C1|generator size calculator]].

faq.q: How many watts does a kVA give?
faq.a: Usable watts are the kVA times one thousand times the power factor, about {{d.pf_generator|pct}} on most sets, so a generator never carries its full kVA figure in watts. [[C7|What a generator can run]] lists the usable watts for each size.

Petrol sets cover the small and middle sizes and cost less to buy; diesel is more common in the larger sizes and uses less fuel per unit of electricity. The [[C8|fuel consumption calculator]] compares the running cost of both.

faq.q: Is a generator cheaper than solar or a UPS for backup?
faq.a: It depends on how many hours of backup you need a year. A generator is cheap to buy and costly to run; the [[N7|UPS vs solar vs generator calculator]] compares the cost per backup hour over the years you pick.
